tr.p0022|35d9d8c40fd78cc0|h: 'The Old Man and the Sea' is a novel written in 1951 by the renowned American author Ernest Hemingway while living in Cuba, and published in 1952. Even though it's a story of a very ordinary fisherman, Ernest Hemingway's 'The Old Man and the Sea' is basically the story of that fisherman's unyielding life. The story goes like this - an elderly fisherman who lives in Cuba, despite his long experience in a fisherman's life, right at the beginning of the story it is known that he hasn't been able to catch a single fish for 84 days in a row. But to him, this failure is not really a failure, rather just another step in the battle of life. He decides that he will go far out into the ocean waters where much bigger fish are found. No sooner thought than done. The next day he sets out for the deep sea and spots the biggest marlin fish he has ever seen in his life. A new dimension of the story begins now with this fish. This dimension describes turning the fish into prey gradually, the fisherman's sacrifice and hardship to catch the fish, and a story developed between the hunter and the hunted during the hunt. It has only 2 main characters. The first main character is Santiago, who is an inhabitant of Cuba and a fisherman by profession, a bit bent under the weight of age, but he has a fantastic pair of eyes in which there is no aging, no tiredness. Santiago's wife has passed away and he is childless. Even after living in extreme poverty, he seems content with life. And the reason for this contentment is his immense knowledge about the sea and fishing. He himself is extremely confident and optimistic. He knows that life means fighting, not necessarily winning that war. He went out with his boat for 84 days but couldn't bring back a single fish. Because of this blame, he turns into the most ill-fated fisherman of his fishing village. But all this couldn't keep him down. He hunted the biggest marlin fish all by himself. He fought continuously for 3 days with nature and his own body to hunt the biggest fish of his life. In the end, whether he succeeded or failed, he wasn't much worried about that, rather his pair of blue eyes held a dream. Besides Santiago, another character in this novel is a boy named Manolin, who used to work on Santiago's boat previously. In the story, this boy is seen as a devotee of Santiago. He used to take care of Santiago, arrange food for him, bring him newspapers, and chat happily with Santiago about American basketball games from old papers. Even though it's a very short story, it seems the author has dragged and made the story much bigger. However, reading this lengthy description makes it clear that the author has extraordinary knowledge about the sea, the lives of fishermen, and their fishing profession. Besides various descriptions of sea life, this story also highlights the real purpose of human life - fighting the battle of life, the relationship between the human community and nature, love for nature, love for life. And the story of an unyielding old fisherman comes up immensely, which teaches us many things. For example: if one's own goal remains firm, it is possible to reach the goal overcoming all obstacles, even if no one is by your side, you must have mental strength and conviction, etc. Therefore, if you ever get depressed on the path of life, you must read this book. Notably, in 1953 'The Old Man and the Sea' won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and in 1954 the Nobel Prize.

tr.p0041|bb8142d37018b4ca|h: ***Book Review*** ***Book name --- Borof Gola Nodi** ***Author --- Zahir Raihan*** ***First publication---1969*** As she was coming close to the house, someone from the two-storied building next door suddenly poured a bucket of water on Mariyam. Her whole body got soaked. For the first few moments Mariyam was completely startled. She had just washed and worn the saree yesterday. Who knows what kind of water it was!!! Thinking about it made her whole body crawl with anger. Father was sitting in the light of the hurricane lamp teaching Khokon. "After Humayun's death, Akbar ascended the throne of Delhi." Mother said, "Mariyam is not around, the house feels so empty. You should get married, Mahmud." Mahmud said, "What is the need to turn another innocent girl into an inhuman monster"? Mansur's eyebrows arched strangely. Then he said slowly, do you think people can fall in love twice? An embarrassed Mariyam said, they can!! "Borof Gola Nodi" is a famous novel written by Zahir Raihan. Set against the backdrop of the seventies, the novel is a saga of helplessness of a decaying middle-class family devastated by economic reasons. ** Central characters of the novel --- Mahmud, Mariyam, Hasina, Lily, Mansur, Taslim, Shahadat, Amena. Mahmud, a boy from a purely middle-class family. He harshly curses the harsh reality of life and the discrimination between rich and poor. He wants to work in the 'Milan' magazine and become an ideal journalist. Someday he will be Louis Fischer!!! But no..... Under the pressure of the prevailing political situation of a corrupt country, his dream soon vanishes. One day he leaves this job.' Mahmud's character is very strange; at the same time harsh and yet soft at moments. Sometimes he scolds his sisters in a harsh voice, and again when his salary increases, he harbors the thought of spending that money for his sisters. Mariyam -- She is Mahmud's younger sister. After taking her Intermediate exams, she is now doing tuition. She has a terrible past of early youth, so she couldn't accept Mansur, the brother-in-law of Selina's (Mariyam's student) sister, easily. Her simple and innocent character fills the reader's heart with sorrow. Lily -- Mariyam's college life friend. tr.p0119|e8cbfebff0a29111|h: Through the everyday snapshot of poor families, the author has portrayed a heart-melting tragedy. An old clerk father, his wife, and five children live in a half-broken house in a dirty little alley. Mahmud is an educated, indomitable yet frustration-ridden young man who, despite being the eldest child, cannot help the family enough with his job and salary. Mariyam is his younger sister, the eldest daughter of the family, who through all her hard work manages her own educational expenses while helping her eighth-grader younger sister Hasina with her demands and financial aid, as well as assisting her mother with household chores. Hasina is a girl at an advanced age, her whims running at a wild pace in tune with her age. Through Mariyam's student Selina, she gets acquainted with Selina's relative Mansur, which unintentionally turns into a liking over time, though Mariyam did not want to move forward with it because of Zahed, her first love and the biggest mistake of her life. Over time, when Mansur's inherent sweetness is liked by everyone in the house, he marries Mariyam, although Mahmud had strong objections because Mansur was rich, as he felt that rich people accumulate influence by sucking the blood of the poor. Just when happy days were about to step into the family with financial support from Mansur, Mansur begins to change when the past relationship between Zahed and Mariyam is revealed to him. In their words—"Does love come twice in a life!" Out of this fear, anger, and resentment, illness descends upon Mariyam's family. As a result, Mansur's promise to build a new house for Mariyam's family remains unfulfilled. When Mariyam returns home, she doesn't let anyone realize about her domestic strife. That very night turns out to be the last night of six sleeping souls filled with heart-full of hopes, due to the collapse of the fragile roof from lack of repair. The parents' hope of getting a new house, Hasina's first letter stirring the light of first love in her life, the hope of clearing mental depression by speaking openly to Mansur—all tear apart as corpses from the pages of life. The relationships that had very little value in Mahmud's life were the pillars he held onto, and even though he never wanted to show it, it didn't remain a secret. Five years later, Mahmud's own family is built through the love and utmost care of Lilly (Mariyam's friend), the co-heroine main character. Selina comes into Mansur's life as the answer to the question he asked Mariyam. Yes, love happens twice in life. It certainly does with Zahir Raiyan and his Borof Gola Nodi.
